sources.entry: LightTable - Digital darkroom and RAW developer with physically modelled film stock simulation.

summary.one_liner: LightTable is a free, GPL-3.0 open-source photo browser and RAW editor with a native macOS app and physically modelled film stock simulation built on spektrafilm.
summary.what_it_does: It browses and organizes photo libraries with ratings, flags, collections, stacks, virtual copies, and keyword and metadata filters, keeping originals separate from edits stored in a SQLite catalog. Its film pipeline simulates 23 film stocks from exposure through print and scan, with grain, halation, and paper controls. The editor adds curves, color grading, local masks, healing, lens correction, crop, and HDR/panorama/focus merge. It can import a copy of a Lightroom Classic catalog, Lightroom XMP, .lrtemplate presets, and Capture One styles, and exports JPEG, PNG, HEIF, or 16-bit TIFF with ICC profiles. It also exposes a local API, a command-line client, and an MCP server.
use_cases: develop RAW photos with film-like looks
organize and rate a photo shoot
convert Lightroom presets to another editor
batch export photos with naming recipes
apply film simulation to digital photos
automate photo edits from the command line
how_to_run: For development, follow the source setup guide in the docs (Python runtime dependencies and pinned film data are required).
Run ./lighttable status --json with the source environment prepared and an app running.
Run ./lighttable photos list --limit 5 --json to list photos.
Run ./lighttable schema to view the API schema.
Use ./lighttable mcp for the stdio MCP server.
notable: Film simulation models stocks, development, paper printing, and scanning using published sensitivity and density data, with measured versus modeled data labeled
Imports a copy of Lightroom Classic catalogs and reports what was mapped or skipped
Local-first design: photos and catalog stay on the machine, with optional on-device Apple Vision tagging
Built-in CLI and MCP server for scripted or agent-driven edits that appear in History with Undo
Interface and Help available in 20 languages
caveats: Not yet publicly released as a desktop app; signed packages are still being prepared and package-manager installers are unavailable.
Native macOS app is the most complete; Windows and Linux support is experimental or lacks public packages, and Linux has no supported release yet.
Source setup requires Python runtime dependencies and pinned film data before first run; the project is in active development.
keywords: develop film look on digital photos
organize photos by rating and keyword
